meta.idAlgorithm: id = 'LL-' + sha256(ruleKey + '|' + path) first 10 hex chars; stable across runs so recurrence is a diff
meta.governance: Only Scot closes a finding, downgrades severity, accepts risk, or sets a disposition (accepted/fixed/dismissed-false-positive/wontfix). closureEvidence.attestation and disposition.decidedBy stay empty until Scot signs. Findings are added mechanically (scripts/audit-merge.rb from /audit-run, scripts/promote-finding.rb from PR-time reviews) and only ever land as status 'open' with disposition 'untriaged'; the adding scripts never close, downgrade, or triage. No student/patient data ever appears here; evidence snippets are code only and any PII/secret-bearing finding is refused at promotion, never redacted-in.
meta.disposition: Optional per-finding triage state, orthogonal to status. status answers 'does the issue still exist in code' (lifecycle, citation-validated); disposition answers 'what did we decide to do about it' (untriaged/accepted/fixed/dismissed-false-positive/wontfix). A finding with no disposition object is treated as untriaged. Set only by Scot.

findings.notes: Surfaced by adversary review of PR #542 (narrowing LL-310b464be4): closing that finding once the legacy protected_image fallback is sunset would otherwise orphan this broader, still-live risk from the register. Filed as its own finding per the adversary's recommendation, since Copilot's 'do not create a duplicate finding' guidance on PR #540/#542 referred to protected_image specifically, not this separate login/lesson/board vector. | TRIAGE DRAFT 2026-07-06 (for Scot's review; disposition intentionally left untriaged): Re-verified every cited line directly against code at the worktree's current HEAD -- user.rb:2632 (user_token), user.rb:2638/2643 (find_by_token, plain `==`, confirmed non-constant-time), lib/json_api/user.rb:41 (login serialization), api/lessons_controller.rb:78/99 (show/complete accept token as sole identity), and all 4 frontend window.open() sites -- all confirmed exactly as described, with one path correction: the boards_controller accept point is app/controllers/boards_controller.rb:101 (the non-API controller), not app/controllers/api/boards_controller.rb as originally drafted. PROPOSED SEVERITY: high (up from medium; see full rationale below) -- this field has been updated to 'high' as a draft recommendation, not a final call; only Scot's disposition decision makes it official. Rationale for high over medium: (1) unlike sibling LL-310b464be4, which covers only a sunsetting legacy fallback (90-day retirement path already underway), user_token is the actively-minted PRIMARY login credential for every user with no deprecation in flight; (2) no per-user revocation exists -- because the token is a pure HMAC of global_id with no per-user secret or version component, it is UNCHANGED by password reset, session invalidation, or any account-compromise remediation available today; only a global GoSecure-verifier-key rotation would invalidate it, which would log out every user simultaneously, so in practice it is never rotated per-incident; (3) broad standing acceptance surface -- 2 backend endpoints treat it as a standalone credential, all 4 frontend window.open() sites place it in a plain navigable URL (browser history + Referer leakage to any third party the destination page loads + server access logs), and login-serializes it to every client on every session; (4) covers FERPA-regulated student lesson/board access with no expiry; (5) comparable precedent already in this register: LL-c6dd65a2aa (static, non-rotating shared cache_token with broad blast radius) was rated high. Countervailing factor keeping this below critical: exploitation still requires actually obtaining a specific user's leaked token (via log/history/Referer exposure or a timing attack against the non-constant-time compare, which needs many low-jitter requests) -- it is not open pre-auth to arbitrary callers the way a critical-rated unauthenticated-disclosure finding (e.g. LL-90137ca466) is. ADDITIONAL SCOPE SURFACED (not yet folded into cited evidence, flagged for follow-up): user_token is also handed in full to third-party embedded integration tools via the embed-frame component (see remediation.options item (c)) -- a distinct exposure path beyond the 4 window.open() sites and 2 controllers currently cited; recommend a short follow-up scoping pass on that path specifically before scheduling remediation option (c). | REMEDIATION 2026-07-09 (option (a), constant-time compare): landed via PR #563, merged to staging as merge commit c0eb0c8b757df2004efe54838abf3c3d706d0852. User.find_by_token now uses ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(hash, verifier) in place of the plain `==`, closing the timing side-channel; behavior-preserving (secure_compare returns false on a length mismatch, does not raise) and covered by two regression specs (valid-token path + same-length wrong-hash mismatch path) in spec/models/user_spec.rb. Dual-reviewer clean: Codex senior-dev Approve and Claude adversary Ship; all CI green (rspec, build-and-test, security-scan, secret-detection, audit-artifacts-integrity). Status intentionally kept open: only phased option (a) is complete; option (b) (~45d purpose-scoped expiring lesson/board share token) and option (c) (user_token expiry/rotation, including the embed-frame third-party exposure surface) remain, and formal closure/severity disposition stays Scot's attestation.

disposition.rationale: Severity promoted medium -> high, approved by Scot 2026-07-08: a permanent, non-revocable HMAC credential exposed through navigable share URLs justifies prioritized remediation. Accepted for remediation on the phased plan: (a) ~7d constant-time comparison hardening in User.find_by_token (ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare); (b) ~45d purpose-scoped expiring lesson/board share-token following the PR #540 protected_image pattern; (c) broader user_token rotation scoped and handled as a separately scoped follow-up.

findings.title: BoardDownstreamButtonSet S3 writes fail against KMS-encrypted bucket: 'Requests specifying Server Side Encryption with AWS KMS managed keys require AWS Signature Version 4'

evidence.source: Resque::Failure diagnostics via a throwaway lingolinq-diagcheck2 Cloud Run Job (rails runner, cloned from lingolinq-web's image/SA/VPC/Cloud SQL/secrets), 2026-07-03
evidence.snippet: 58 of 914 Resque::Failure entries are BoardDownstreamButtonSet#perform_action failing with the raw S3 API error body: 'InvalidArgumentRequests specifying Server Side Encryption with AWS KMS managed keys require AWS Signature Version 4.Authorization...'. Traced to the actual upload path: lib/uploader.rb Uploader.remote_upload (line 46) calls remote_upload_params (line 293), which hand-builds a browser-style S3 POST policy signed with SigV2 (AWSAccessKeyId + base64 policy + HMAC-SHA1 signature via OpenSSL::HMAC.digest('sha1', ...), lines 296-334) and posts it directly with Typhoeus.post (line 68) - this path does not go through Aws::S3::Client at all, so an aws-sdk-s3 signature_version config has no effect on it. This is a genuine request-signing misconfiguration, independent of the OOM-driven SIGKILL failures (LL-a95e9c5f7c) and independent of the pre-existing ImageMagick/job_stash failures (LL-5954bcbbe6).

remediation.options: Codex review of PR #516 correctly caught two rounds of an inaccurate fix here: first, that the original remediation (bump signature_version on an Aws::S3::Client) targets a client this code path never uses; second, that the corrected suggestion (Aws::S3::Presigner#presigned_post) names a method that doesn't exist on the installed aws-sdk-s3 1.219.0 - Presigner only exposes presigned_url/presigned_request. POST-policy signing lives on the separate Aws::S3::PresignedPost class (lib/aws-sdk-s3/presigned_post.rb), normally reached via the Aws::S3::Bucket resource's presigned_post(options) method (lib/aws-sdk-s3/customizations/bucket.rb:126-133), which builds one from the client's credentials/region/bucket name. Replace the handcrafted SigV2 POST policy in Uploader.remote_upload_params (lib/uploader.rb:293-336) with a PresignedPost built this way (either via Aws::S3::Resource.new(...).bucket(name).presigned_post(...) or Aws::S3::PresignedPost.new(credentials, region, bucket_name, options) directly) - it produces the same browser-postable form-field shape (key/policy/x-amz-* fields) but signed AWS4-HMAC-SHA256, satisfying the KMS-SSE bucket's SigV4 requirement. Verify against the bucket's policy that SSE-KMS enforcement is intended, then re-run the affected board's button-set update and confirm Resque::Failure stops accumulating this error.

closureEvidence.verifierNote: Code-remediated on scot/fix/worker-pool-oom-sigv4: Uploader.remote_upload_params (lib/uploader.rb:293-336, formerly hand-signed SigV2) rewritten to build an Aws::S3::PresignedPost(credentials, region, bucket_name, key:, content_type:, content_length_range:, success_action_status:, acl:) directly, producing an AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-signed POST policy (x-amz-credential/x-amz-algorithm/x-amz-date/x-amz-signature fields) that satisfies SSE-KMS buckets' SigV4 requirement, exactly matching the remediation option's guidance (Aws::S3::PresignedPost, not the nonexistent Presigner#presigned_post). Codex review of this PR (#521) caught a follow-on regression in the first pass (commit 77233fb19): returning the PresignedPost's own regional endpoint as upload_url broke every consumer that pattern-matches a stored self.url against the static global s3.amazonaws.com form (valid_import_bundle_url?, removable_remote_url?, fronted_url, remote_remove, and every *_controller.rb upload_success action). Fixed in afe03d2de: remote_upload_params now returns both upload_url (unchanged canonical global form, for URL construction/matching) and a new post_url (the regional SigV4 POST target); the three Typhoeus.post call sites and two frontend POST targets (content-grabbers.js, beta-feedback-form.js, with a post_url || upload_url fallback) now use post_url. spec/lib/uploader_spec.rb and spec/models/concerns/uploadable_spec.rb updated to assert the split shape; full uploader/uploadable/button_sound/beta_feedback_recording/extra_data/logs/sounds spec suites green except two pre-existing unrelated test-DB-pollution failures (ButtonImage.count inflated by orphaned committed rows; an unrelated GoSecure OpenSSL 'bad decrypt' on cached_copy; a boards_controller_spec BoardLocale.count leak - all three reproduce in isolation on main, unrelated to this change). Not yet live-verified: requires redeploying the rehearsal image and confirming Resque::Failure stops accumulating the KMS-SSE SigV4 error on the next BoardDownstreamButtonSet run, plus a bucket-policy check that SSE-KMS enforcement on this bucket is actually intended. End-to-end synthetic verification: a real ButtonImage (id 840) processed by the live worker pool landed in the bucket (224566 bytes, image/png, ServerSideEncryption aws:kms under the expected CMK); record destroy also removed the S3 object. Read path: CloudFront distribution E2X2HAS6Y1L2MI (OAC, bucket-policy + KMS key-policy grants scoped to the distribution ARN) fronts the bucket; UPLOADS_S3_CDN set on both stacks 2026-07-05. findings.title: A diagnostic SES send to a personal Gmail address never arrived (inbox or spam); a same-account send to a Workspace-internal address arrived immediately

evidence.source: Two live Aws::SES::Client#send_email diagnostics against the same lingolinq-prod SES account/region (us-west-2), 2026-07-03/04. First: a direct-API send to a personal scotwahlquist@gmail.com address (PR #516/#521 0a rehearsal follow-up) returned a real SES MessageId but the recipient confirmed it never arrived in Inbox or Spam. Second (this finding): a retest send to the Workspace-internal beta@lingolinq.com alias (subject "GCP rehearsal SES diag retest (beta@ alias, direct-api)", MessageId 0101019f2a7d6e11-c08396d5-591f-4c0b-95b3-5a83a49e6d57-000000) landed in scot@lingolinq.com's Inbox (not Spam) within seconds of sending.
evidence.snippet: Live SESv2 GetAccount/GetEmailIdentity checks at time of diagnosis: account ProductionAccessEnabled=true, EnforcementStatus=HEALTHY, TRANSACTIONAL use case approved (Details.ReviewDetails.Status=GRANTED); lingolinq.com domain identity VerificationStatus=SUCCESS, DkimAttributes.Status=SUCCESS (Easy DKIM, RSA_2048_BIT); scotwahlquist@gmail.com is NOT on the account suppression list (GetSuppressedDestination -> NotFoundException). CORRECTION (caught by Codex review of this PR, verified against AWS's own API docs before accepting): GetSendStatistics.DeliveryAttempts is documented as "Number of emails that have been sent" -- an account-wide 15-minute aggregate of SES send attempts, NOT a per-message delivery-to-recipient-MTA confirmation. The 2026-07-03T16:47:00Z data point (2 DeliveryAttempts, 0 Bounces, 0 Complaints, 0 Rejects) only shows SES accepted the API call and recorded no account-wide hard bounce in that window; it does NOT prove Gmail's MTA received or processed this specific message, and does not by itself support a conclusion of Gmail-side filtering over any other cause. A live telemetry check on 2026-07-04 found zero SES configuration sets, Virtual Deliverability Manager disabled, and no identity-level delivery-notification topic for lingolinq.com, so no retained per-message delivery event is available for either diagnostic send. Future per-message delivery confirmation requires an SES configuration set with an event destination that carries per-message records (SNS, Amazon Data Firehose, or EventBridge -- plain CloudWatch only publishes aggregate metrics, not per-message events) or Virtual Deliverability Manager enabled before a new test. Separately (and this part is a genuine, confirmed gap, independent of the delivery-attempts question above): MailFromAttributes has no custom MailFromDomain configured -- SES is using its default amazonses.com bounce/Return-Path domain rather than a lingolinq.com subdomain, so SPF does not align with the From: domain (DKIM alignment alone is presumably covering DMARC today, since the domain already has DMARC aggregate reporting flowing to Google/Microsoft). This is worthwhile SPF-alignment hardening on its own merits, not a proven cause of the non-delivery.

remediation.options: (a) Obtain per-message delivery evidence before assigning root cause: enable an SES configuration set with an event destination that carries per-message delivery/bounce/complaint records -- SNS, Amazon Data Firehose, or EventBridge (plain CloudWatch only publishes aggregate metrics/counts, not per-message events, so it would not satisfy this) -- or enable Virtual Deliverability Manager, then re-run the scotwahlquist@gmail.com send and read the actual event for that specific MessageId. (b) Configure a custom MAIL FROM domain (e.g. mail.lingolinq.com) on the SES domain identity so SPF aligns with the From: domain in addition to DKIM -- worthwhile hardening regardless of whether it turns out to be the cause here. (c) Enable the SES deliverability dashboard (currently off) and/or enroll lingolinq.com in Google Postmaster Tools for real external-Gmail reputation signal. (d) Re-test sends to 2-3 different personal-email providers (Gmail, Outlook.com/Hotmail, Yahoo) to determine whether this is Gmail-specific or a broader personal-inbox gap, using (a)'s per-message tracking so the result is actually conclusive this time.

The confirmed, undisputed fact remains: the original send to scotwahlquist@gmail.com never arrived (inbox or spam checked), while a same-account retest to a Workspace-internal address arrived immediately -- the open question is root cause, not whether a real gap exists. The message addressed directly to scotwahlquist@gmail.com was searched for across inbox/spam/trash (`in:anywhere`, `includeTrash:true`) and found nowhere -- reproducing the non-delivery exactly, now through ActionMailer rather than the raw SDK. This partially closes the 'was this just a raw-SDK artifact' question (adapter-level, not yet mailer-class-level) but does not change the underlying open root-cause question (still no per-message delivery event tracking exists to say why Gmail specifically drops it); remediation options (a)-(d) above remain the path forward.

findings.notes: Surfaced by Codex's senior-dev review (/review-pr) of PR #535 (LL-1890f6a922, DataPolicyEnforcer retention scope): extending the retention purge to LogSession log_type 'profile' would delete the source record while UserExtra#process_profile's cached identifiable summary (template_id, summary, summary_color, log_id) and the mirrored UserLink.data['state']['profile_history'] entry are never refreshed on destroy, so identifiable content would persist in those caches after the source log is gone -- worse than the pre-existing status quo of not purging 'profile' at all. PR #535 responded by dropping 'profile' from DataPolicyEnforcer::RETAINABLE_LOG_TYPES (lib/data_policy_enforcer.rb) rather than shipping a half-fixed purge; this finding tracks the cache-invalidation work needed before 'profile' can safely be added back. Checked note/assessment/eval/journal for the same pattern: none found (user_badge.rb's assessment usage re-queries live LogSession rows on demand rather than caching a summary; weekly_stats_summary.rb caches only session_ids, not identifiable content, and per DATA_RETENTION.md's Analytics events row this is documented/accepted since aggregates 'do not re-identify individuals').

findings.title: DataPolicyEnforcer retention job skips child orgs that inherit (rather than set) a retention_months policy

remediation.options: Organization#effective_data_policy (app/models/organization.rb:81-101) is explicitly designed to inherit retention_months from a parent org, but enforce_retention!'s candidate-org WHERE clause only matches orgs whose OWN data_policy_version is > 0, and then only sweeps that org's own sponsored_users. A child org that never set its own policy (data_policy_version stays 0) is skipped by the WHERE clause entirely, even though its users are governed by an inherited window via a parent's policy -- so their communication logs never expire. Widen the candidate set to include any org whose effective (not just own) retention_months resolves to a positive value -- e.g. iterate every org with a policy-bearing ancestor, or drive the sweep off each org's own effective_data_policy rather than gating the WHERE clause on data_policy_version. Add a parent(policy)+child(data_policy_version 0) spec asserting the child's stale logs are purged.

findings.notes: Surfaced by adversary review of PR #535 (LL-1890f6a922, DataPolicyEnforcer log_type scope). Pre-existing since before that PR -- it changed only the log_type filter inside the loop, not the org-selection WHERE clause or the sponsored_users scoping -- but it directly undermines LL-1890f6a922's storage-limitation objective: an org hierarchy where only the parent sets retention_months leaves every child org's logs permanently unenforced. Confirmed against Organization#effective_data_policy's inheritance logic (organization.rb:84-96), which resolves retention_months from a parent for exactly this configuration, and against Organization#sponsored_users (organization.rb:677-685), which is scoped to one org's own attached users, not any descendant org's users.

findings.title: Retention purge deletes the LogSession's PaperTrail destroy-version and writes no disposal AuditEvent

remediation.options: Flusher.flush_record (lib/flusher.rb) destroys the record (creating a has_paper_trail :on => [:destroy] version, log_session.rb:24) and then immediately delete_alls that same version via flush_versions, and DataPolicyEnforcer.enforce_retention! writes no AuditEvent for its purges at all -- unlike Flusher.flush_leftovers, which records a per-category AuditEvent for its deletions (lib/flusher.rb ~line 224). This contradicts docs/legal/DATA_RETENTION.md row 30 (Authentication and audit trails / PaperTrail versions on User, Board, LogSession retained 6 years, HIPAA 45 CFR Sec 164.316(b)(2)(i)) and leaves no record proving what data was destroyed, when, or by which policy. Either stop deleting the destroy-version for LogSession specifically in this retention path (retain per row 30), or have enforce_retention! emit a per-run AuditEvent (actor 'system', org id, purged log ids/counts) the way flush_leftovers already does, so a HIPAA access-log review can reconstruct the disposal.

findings.notes: Surfaced by adversary review of PR #535 (LL-1890f6a922, DataPolicyEnforcer log_type scope). Pre-existing since before that PR -- Flusher.flush_record's destroy-then-delete-versions behavior and enforce_retention!'s lack of an AuditEvent call are both unchanged by it -- but PR #535 widens the set of log_types this same behavior applies to from 1 (session) to 4 (session/note/assessment/eval/journal), modestly increasing real-world exposure. No user impact today (prod/staging carry no real users, per project note), but this needs resolving before onboarding real school-district/hospital users, since the retention job is precisely the mechanism DATA_RETENTION.md documents as satisfying GDPR 5(1)(e) storage limitation, and doing so by destroying the very audit trail row 30 requires keeping for 6 years is an internal contradiction in the documented schedule, not just a code gap.

findings.title: Org retention policy purges a sponsored user's entire log history, including logs outside that org's context

remediation.options: Confirm with Scot whether an org's retention_months is meant to reach a sponsored user's entire log history (including logs predating enrollment, or generated under a personal/other-org context), or only logs created within that org's context. Today the query is user_id-scoped only, with no org/context filter, so any sponsoring org that sets retention_months deletes all of that user's aged logs regardless of origin -- for a user sponsored by more than one org, the most-aggressive policy effectively wins for their whole history. If the current behavior is intentional, document it explicitly in DATA_RETENTION.md's LogSession row rather than leaving it implicit; if not, scope the purge query by log ownership/context (e.g. author's org at the time, or a recorded originating-org field).

findings.notes: Surfaced by adversary review of PR #535 (LL-1890f6a922, DataPolicyEnforcer log_type scope). Pre-existing since before that PR -- the user_id-only scoping is unchanged, and PR #535 only widened the log_type filter -- but broadening the purge to 4 additional log_types (note/assessment/eval/journal) means more of a cross-context user's history is now reachable by this same scoping gap than before. This is data over-deletion risk, not a data leak, and is plausibly by design (retention as a property of the user's relationship to a sponsoring org); flagged as a design question for Scot rather than asserted as a defect.

remediation.options: When Organization#remove_user calls License#release_user!
